title: VPC batching & cache recommendations: offline simulator + guarded apply playbook
creator: Sameer Kaur
description:
Goal: Build an offline-safe simulation runner and operator playbook that generates batching and prefix/KV cache recommendations for Private/VPC/on-prem customers, validates those changes against policy gates, estimates cost/latency impact using recorded traffic, and produces an auditable guarded-apply that can be executed or rolled back with minimal blast radius.

Background: For private deployments we cannot perform live autosuggest/config changes without explicit customer approval and audit. Customers also require an offline mode for air-gapped installs and explicit policy enforcement (allowed quantization levels, approved instance shapes, KMS usage). Current advisors produce recommendations but lack a sandboxed, reproducible verification step and a standardized guarded-apply flow for VPC/private customers.

This ticket covers: the simulation runner (runs recommendations against replayed request traces), a decision playbook (how to choose safe defaults and thresholds), policy gate integration (policy engine + whitelist/blacklist for quantization/batching kernels), and a guarded apply CLI/UI that records a dry-run, an apply plan, and a rollback plan with audit log entries.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator accepts 7-day request trace sample and emits per-variant cost delta and median/95th latency projection
Offline mode runs without external network access and relies only on local KMS stub and recorded telemetry
Policy gates prevent recommendations that violate customer constraints (e.g., disallowed INT8 quantization, restricted instance families)
Guarded-apply produces a human-readable plan + machine-checksumed artifacts and can be executed in dry-run or apply mode
Rollback plan is auto-generated and verified by the simulator to restore prior batching/cache config within target SLOs
All simulation runs and applies surface an audit bundle (commit id, inputs, metrics, approver) persisted to the customer audit log
tasks: Design simulator schema for replay input, control knobs (batch size, batch timeout, prefix cache hit policy, kv cache TTL)
Add local KMS stub and configuration profiles for offline runs
Implement policy engine adapters: allowed_quantizations, allowed_instance_families, network_restrictions
Integrate cost model (tokenized cost per op + GPU pricing overrides) into simulator
Create CLI 'ri-sim' with commands: plan, simulate, diff, guarded-apply, rollback
Wire simulator outputs to Console UI: proposed changes, cost delta, risk score, artifacts download
Add audit bundle builder and S3/GCS-like local store for private deployments
Write e2e test harness using pre-captured traces and synthetic SLO regressions
risks_and_tradeoffs: Accuracy vs speed: detailed KV-level simulation is more accurate but expensive; we'll default to stratified sampling of traces for full replay
Estimator correctness: cost model must be conservative for customer safety; initial model will overestimate savings by 5-10% to avoid surprise
Offline limitations: some telemetry signals (live device temps, ephemeral kernel metrics) are unavailable offline — fallback to historical heuristics
Policy complexity: too-strict policies will suppress legitimate savings; include a policy-explain step so PMs/SEs can iterate with customers
implementation_notes: Simulator to reuse existing batching simulator library but extend to support KV cache TTL and prefix eviction policies
Record a compact plan manifest: {inputs:trace_id, config_delta, cost_projection, latency_projection, checksum} (manifest stored as newline-delimited JSON in audit bundle)
Guarded-apply will be a two-phase operation: upload plan -> customer (or SE) approval -> orchestrator executes apply in isolated canary -> monitor SLOs -> promote or rollback
For on-prem we will provide a binary mode of ri-sim that writes artifacts to a mounted path; integrate with Confluent-style connectors for local storage
Add CORS-safe console endpoints for Private Console; ensure policy evaluation happens server-side with customer policy files pulled from their VCS (read-only)
notes: Contact SE owners: Priya Das (se-priya@redwood.ai) for customer approval flow details
